---
title: "Ordinal and categorical responses"
author: "Dongwen Luo"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.align = "center", fig.width = 7,
                      fig.height = 3.5)
```

```{r setup}
library(predictmeans)
library(ggplot2)
```

A response that is a class (a rating 1 to 5, low/medium/high satisfaction, a colour) has no single mean.
`predictmeans()` gives means on the scale each model has, and the class probabilities on request.

| model | fitted by | means (default) | other `mean_type` |
|---|---|---|---|
| cumulative link, parallel slopes | `MASS::polr`, `ordinal::clm`, `ordinal::clmm`, `VGAM::vglm(cumulative / propodds / acat / cratio / sratio, parallel = TRUE)` | the latent scale: one mean per level | `"prob"` and `"mean_class"` add a table of class probabilities or the mean class |
| multinomial, slopes that are not parallel, or scale effects | `nnet::multinom`, `VGAM::vglm(multinomial)`, `vglm(..., parallel = FALSE)`, `clm(..., nominal = , scale = )` | `"prob"`: each class probability, compared within its class | `"prob_diff"`, `"link"`, `"mean_class"` (ordinal families) |

All tests are z tests (these models have no dispersion to estimate), except `clmm`, which uses the
inner-outer df of other mixed models.

## Parallel slopes: one latent scale

The wine data (`ordinal`): bitterness rated 1 to 5 by 9 judges, at two temperatures and with or without
contact.

```{r}
data(wine, package = "ordinal")
m <- ordinal::clm(rating ~ temp + contact, data = wine)
pm <- predictmeans(m, "temp:contact", pairwise = TRUE)
summary(pm)
```

The means are on the latent scale, x'b minus the mean cut point (emmeans' `mode = "latent"`). A difference
of 2.5 between warm and cold is a log odds ratio: at every cut point the odds of a higher rating are
exp(2.5) = 12 times larger when warm. The same model by `polr()` or `vglm(propodds)` gives the same means.

The class probabilities of each mean:

```{r}
pp <- predictmeans(m, "temp:contact", mean_type = "prob")
head(pp$probs, 5)
predictmeans(m, "temp:contact", mean_type = "mean_class")$probs
```

The mean class scores the classes 1, 2, 3, ... as equally spaced; the advice says so.

### Judges as random effects

```{r}
mm <- ordinal::clmm(rating ~ temp + contact + (1 | judge), data = wine)
pmm <- predictmeans(mm, "temp", mean_type = "prob")
pmm$means[, c("temp", "estimate", "std.error", "df")]
advice(pmm)$text
```

The means are for a typical judge (random effects at 0), and so are the class probabilities: averaged over
judges they are less extreme. `bias_adjust = TRUE` gives those averages (the population-average
probabilities, integrated over the random effects), with SEs that include the uncertainty of the judges'
variance:

```{r}
predictmeans(mm, "temp", mean_type = "prob", bias_adjust = TRUE)$probs
```

The pairs stay on the latent scale: comparisons for a judge, the same for every judge. The df are
inner-outer: with few judges, z tests reject a true null too often (11% at the 5% level with 6 clusters in a
simulation).

## Multinomial and non-parallel fits: class probabilities

Satisfaction with housing (`MASS::housing`, counts in `Freq`):

```{r}
data(housing, package = "MASS")
mh <- nnet::multinom(Sat ~ Infl + Type + Cont, weights = Freq, data = housing, trace = FALSE)
ph <- predictmeans(mh, "Infl", pairwise = TRUE)
summary(ph)
```

Each class probability is a mean; the class (`Sat`) is a factor of the means, and the pairs are within each
class. By default the probabilities are compared on the logit scale, as a binomial glm: the limits stay
inside 0 to 1, and a pair is the odds ratio of that class against all the others (not the model's
coefficients, which compare classes with the reference class). With two classes the results are those of
the binomial glm.

```{r, fig.height = 3}
autoplot(ph, scale = "response")
```

Differences of probabilities, as emmeans' `mode = "prob"`:

```{r}
pd <- predictmeans(mh, "Infl", mean_type = "prob_diff")
head(pd$pairs[, c("level1", "level2", "by", "estimate", "std.error", "p.value")], 3)
```

For two means these differences sum to zero over the classes. Near 0 or 1 they are less exact than the
logit-scale tests; the advice says so when it applies.

The model's own linear predictors (`mean_type = "link"`) give exact Wald tests on the model scale, but for a
multinomial model each depends on the reference class.

A non-parallel cumulative fit (the effect of influence differs between cut points) gives the same tables, and
also the mean class:

```{r}
vh <- VGAM::vglm(Sat ~ Infl + Type + Cont, VGAM::cumulative(parallel = FALSE ~ Infl), weights = Freq,
                 data = housing)
predictmeans(vh, "Infl", mean_type = "mean_class")$means
```

`clm()` fits the same non-parallel model with `nominal =`, and with `scale =` a spread of the latent variable
for each level of a factor (then the latent means of two levels are not on one scale, and the class
probabilities are the means):

```{r}
ch <- ordinal::clm(Sat ~ Type + Cont, nominal = ~ Infl, scale = ~ Type, weights = Freq, data = housing)
predictmeans(ch, "Infl")$means[, c("Infl", "Sat", "response", "response.conf.low", "response.conf.high")]
```

## Things predictmeans checks

- **Averaging over other factors.** Class probabilities are averaged over the other factors on the
  probability scale (the share of each class over their levels), as emmeans. For parallel models the
  latent means are averaged instead and then turned into probabilities.
- **Separation.** A class with no observations at some level puts its probability at 0, where the
  standard errors are not usable; a caution names the classes and levels.
- **Crossing curves.** In non-parallel cumulative fits the cumulative curves can cross, giving negative
  probabilities at some levels or covariate values. Means that use such a point are NA, with a caution;
  the other means are kept.
- **Aggregated counts.** With `weights = "proportional"` the factor combinations are weighted by their
  number of cases (the sums of `Freq` here), so aggregated data and one row per case agree.
- **Not available.** `trans`, `vcov` and `permlist` stop for these models, and `bias_adjust` except for
  the class probabilities of `clmm` (population averages, random intercepts), and
  `contrastmeans()`, `covariatemeans()`, `residplot()` and others stop for multinomial and non-parallel fits
  and for `clm` with nominal or scale effects.

## Checks

- Latent means, pairs and class probabilities equal emmeans to 1e-6 (`polr`, `clm`, `clmm`). Population-average
  `clmm` probabilities are computed by adaptive numerical integration, accurate to about 1e-10 for any
  random-effect SD and link (tested at SD 1.1 and 5 with logit and cloglog); for a probit link they equal the
  closed form Phi((theta - x'b) / sqrt(1 + s^2)); their SEs equal a numerical delta method.
- `clm` and `vglm` against SAS PROC LOGISTIC and GLIMMIX (logit, probit, cloglog, adjacent-category; class
  probabilities to 4e-7).
- `multinom` class probabilities, SEs and both kinds of pairs equal emmeans to 1e-8; `vglm(multinomial)`
  equals `multinom`; non-parallel `cumulative`, `cratio` and `sratio` equal `predict()` with SEs by a
  numerical delta method. `clm` with nominal or scale effects (logit, probit; flexible or equidistant cut
  points) equals `predict.clm(type = "prob", se.fit = TRUE)` to 1e-8, and its nominal fits equal
  `vglm(cumulative(parallel = FALSE ~ z))` (SEs within 2%: vglm uses the expected information).

The tests are in `tests/testthat/test-ordinal.R`, `test-ordinal-sas.R` and `test-categorical.R`.
